title: Claude Cowork virtual machine
what: A Linux virtual machine the Claude app downloads to run Cowork (agent) tasks. Usually around 10 GB.
ifDeleted: Claude downloads it again the next time you use Cowork. Anything saved only inside the virtual machine is lost.
howToClean: Quit Claude first, then move claudevm.bundle to the Trash. If you use Cowork every day it will just come back.

title: Claude Code chat history
what: Saved transcripts of your Claude Code conversations, one folder per project.
ifDeleted: Those conversations can no longer be resumed or searched. Your code is not affected.
howToClean: Delete folders for projects you're done with. Claude Code also removes old chats itself after cleanupPeriodDays (set in ~/.claude/settings.json).

title: Codex chat history
what: Saved transcripts of your Codex sessions.
ifDeleted: Those sessions can no longer be resumed. Your code is not affected.

title: Git history
what: The full version history of a code project.
ifDeleted: The project loses its history and any commits you haven't pushed. The current files stay.

title: Node.js packages
what: Packages downloaded for a JavaScript project.
ifDeleted: Run npm install (or pnpm, yarn or bun install) in the project to get them back. Old projects you no longer open are the easiest wins.

title: Build output
what: Files a build tool generates from your source code.
ifDeleted: Rebuilt the next time you build or run the project.

title: Python virtual environment
owner: The Python project it sits in
what: The Python packages installed for one project.
ifDeleted: The project won't run until you recreate it.
howToClean: Recreate it later with `uv sync`, or `python -m venv .venv` and `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

title: App cache
owner: The app named in the path (Chrome, Slack, Discord, VS Code, Claude and other web-based apps)
what: Images, scripts and compiled code the app keeps so it starts and loads faster.
ifDeleted: The app rebuilds it as you use it. Sign-ins and settings are kept.
howToClean: Quit the app first. Many apps also have a Clear Cache option in their settings.

title: Spotify offline cache
what: Songs Spotify keeps on disk so they play instantly.
ifDeleted: Spotify streams them again. Downloaded playlists may need downloading again.
howToClean: Spotify › Settings › Storage › Clear cache.

title: Editor per-project state
what: What the editor remembers per project: open tabs, search indexes, extension data.
ifDeleted: Projects reopen without their previous tabs and per-project extension state. Indexes rebuild.

title: Xcode build data
what: Build output and code indexes for your Xcode projects.
ifDeleted: Xcode rebuilds it the next time you build. The first build is slower.

title: Xcode archives
what: Builds you archived for the App Store or for sharing, with their debug symbols.
ifDeleted: You can't re-export those builds or read crash reports from them. Keep archives of versions people still use.
howToClean: Xcode › Window › Organizer › Archives, delete old ones there.

title: Device debug symbols
what: Debug symbols Xcode copies from each iPhone, iPad or Watch OS version you've connected.
ifDeleted: Xcode copies them again the next time you connect a device with that OS version.

title: Xcode previews and docs cache
what: Files Xcode generates for SwiftUI previews and documentation.
ifDeleted: Xcode generates them again when needed.

title: Simulator caches
what: Temporary files the iOS Simulator keeps.
ifDeleted: Rebuilt the next time you run a simulator.

title: Simulator devices
what: Your simulated iPhones and iPads, with the apps and data installed on them.
ifDeleted: Those simulators and their app data are gone. Xcode can create fresh ones.
howToClean: Run `xcrun simctl delete unavailable` to remove simulators for OS versions you no longer have, or use Xcode › Window › Devices and Simulators.

title: Simulator runtimes
what: One full copy of iOS, watchOS or visionOS for each simulator version you downloaded.
ifDeleted: You can't run simulators for that version until you download it again.
howToClean: Xcode › Settings › Components: delete versions you don't test on.

title: iPhone and iPad backups
what: Backups of your iPhone or iPad made on this Mac.
ifDeleted: You can't restore your device from that backup. Fine if you use iCloud Backup or have a newer one.
howToClean: Finder › select your device › Manage Backups, and delete old ones there.

title: Device firmware
what: Firmware for an iPhone, iPad or Mac, kept after an update or restore.
ifDeleted: Apple downloads it again if it's ever needed.

title: Installer or disk image
what: Usually an installer you downloaded to set up an app.
ifDeleted: Nothing breaks if the app is already installed. Some .dmg files are encrypted disk images with your own files inside, so open it first if you're not sure.

title: Docker Desktop disk
what: Docker's virtual disk. Every image, container and volume lives in one big file (Docker.raw).
ifDeleted: Deleting it directly wipes all images, containers and volumes, including databases you run in Docker.
howToClean: Run `docker system prune -a` to remove unused images and stopped containers (add --volumes for unused volumes), or Docker Desktop › Troubleshoot › Clean / Purge data.

title: OrbStack containers and machines
what: OrbStack's disk with your Docker images, containers, volumes and Linux machines.
ifDeleted: All of them are wiped.
howToClean: Run `docker system prune -a`, or delete machines and images inside OrbStack.

title: Colima / Lima virtual machines
what: Linux virtual machines that run your containers.
ifDeleted: The machines and every container image inside them are gone.
howToClean: Run `docker system prune -a` to clear unused images, or `colima delete` to remove a machine you no longer use.

title: Virtual machine
what: A whole computer's disk stored as files.
ifDeleted: The virtual machine and everything inside it are gone.
howToClean: Delete VMs you don't use from inside Parallels, UTM or VMware. Parallels can also reclaim unused space inside a VM's disk.

title: Hugging Face models
what: AI models and datasets downloaded by Python code.
ifDeleted: They download again the next time code asks for them, which can be many GB.
howToClean: Run `huggingface-cli delete-cache` to pick which models to remove.

title: Ollama models
what: Local AI models you pulled with Ollama.
ifDeleted: Those models have to be downloaded again with `ollama pull`.
howToClean: Run `ollama list` to see models and `ollama rm <name>` to remove ones you don't use.

title: LM Studio models
what: Local AI models downloaded in LM Studio.
ifDeleted: Those models have to be downloaded again.
howToClean: LM Studio › My Models: delete models you don't use.

title: Homebrew downloads
what: Installers Homebrew downloaded.
ifDeleted: Homebrew downloads them again if needed.
howToClean: Run `brew cleanup --prune=all`.

title: Homebrew packages
what: Command-line tools and apps installed with Homebrew.
ifDeleted: Installed tools stop working.
howToClean: Run `brew cleanup` to remove old versions and `brew autoremove` for unused dependencies. Remove tools with `brew uninstall`.

title: npm cache
what: Copies of every package npm has downloaded.
ifDeleted: npm downloads packages again on the next install.
howToClean: Run `npm cache clean --force`.

title: pnpm package store
what: The shared package store pnpm links into your projects.
ifDeleted: pnpm downloads packages again. Existing projects may need `pnpm install`.
howToClean: Run `pnpm store prune` to remove only packages no project uses.

title: Yarn cache
what: Copies of packages Yarn has downloaded.
ifDeleted: Yarn downloads packages again on the next install.
howToClean: Run `yarn cache clean`.

title: Bun cache
what: Copies of packages Bun has downloaded.
ifDeleted: Bun downloads packages again on the next install.
howToClean: Run `bun pm cache rm`.

title: Python package cache
what: Copies of Python packages pip or uv downloaded.
ifDeleted: They download again on the next install.
howToClean: Run `pip cache purge` or `uv cache clean`.

title: Python installations
what: Python versions and conda environments.
ifDeleted: Projects that use them stop working until you recreate the environment.
howToClean: Remove ones you don't use with `pyenv uninstall <version>` or `conda env remove -n <name>`. `conda clean --all` clears conda's download cache.

title: Gradle cache
what: Downloaded dependencies and Gradle versions.
ifDeleted: Downloaded again on the next build, which is slower.

title: Maven repository
what: Java libraries Maven downloaded.
ifDeleted: Downloaded again on the next build.

title: Cargo cache
what: Rust crates Cargo downloaded.
ifDeleted: Downloaded again on the next build.

title: Rust toolchains
what: Installed Rust compiler versions.
ifDeleted: Projects pinned to that version won't build until it's reinstalled.
howToClean: Run `rustup toolchain list`, then `rustup toolchain uninstall <name>` for old ones.

title: Go module cache
what: Go modules downloaded for your projects.
ifDeleted: Downloaded again on the next build.
howToClean: Run `go clean -modcache`. These files are read-only, so the Trash may refuse them.

title: Android emulator images
what: Android emulator system images and virtual devices.
ifDeleted: Those emulators stop working until you download the images again.
howToClean: Android Studio › Device Manager to delete devices, and SDK Manager to remove system images.

title: Android SDK
what: Android build tools and platform files.
ifDeleted: Android projects won't build until Android Studio downloads it again.
howToClean: Remove old platforms and build tools in Android Studio › SDK Manager.

title: Editor extensions
what: Extensions installed in your code editor.
ifDeleted: The editor loses those extensions until you reinstall them.
howToClean: Uninstall extensions you don't use from the editor's Extensions panel.

title: WhatsApp data
what: WhatsApp chats and the photos, videos and documents it downloaded.
ifDeleted: Chats and media that aren't backed up are lost from this Mac.
howToClean: Delete large media from inside WhatsApp.

title: Telegram data
what: Telegram's cached photos, videos and files.
ifDeleted: Telegram downloads media again from the cloud when you open a chat.
howToClean: Use Telegram's storage settings to clear cached media.

title: Messages attachments
what: Photos, videos and files sent and received in Messages.
ifDeleted: They disappear from your conversations on this Mac.
howToClean: System Settings › General › Storage › Messages lets you review large attachments, or set Messages › Settings › Keep messages to 1 Year.

title: Messages history
what: Your iMessage and SMS conversations.
ifDeleted: Conversations not in iCloud are lost.

title: Mail data
what: Email and attachments Mail has downloaded.
ifDeleted: Mail has to download everything again, and messages stored only on this Mac are lost.
howToClean: Delete large emails in Mail, or remove accounts you don't use.

title: Photos library
what: Your photo and video library.
ifDeleted: Photos that aren't in iCloud Photos or another backup are lost forever.
howToClean: Turn on iCloud Photos with Optimize Mac Storage (Photos › Settings › iCloud), or delete photos in Photos and then empty Recently Deleted.

title: Final Cut Pro library
what: Your Final Cut projects, media, renders and proxies.
ifDeleted: Your projects are gone.
howToClean: In Final Cut Pro, select the library and choose File › Delete Generated Library Files to remove render and proxy files.

title: Logic / GarageBand sounds
what: Instrument sounds and loops.
ifDeleted: Projects that use those sounds play silence until you download them again.
howToClean: In Logic Pro: Logic Pro › Sound Library › Sound Library Manager.

title: Steam games
what: Games installed through Steam.
ifDeleted: The games have to be downloaded again.
howToClean: Uninstall games from your Steam library.

title: iCloud Drive
what: iCloud Drive files that are downloaded to this Mac.
ifDeleted: Deleting here deletes them from iCloud and all your devices.
howToClean: Turn on Optimize Mac Storage (System Settings › Apple Account › iCloud › iCloud Drive), or right-click big files in Finder › Remove Download.

title: Cloud drive
owner: Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive or Box
what: Files your cloud drive keeps synced on this Mac.
ifDeleted: Deleting here deletes them from the cloud and your other devices too.
howToClean: Right-click files › Remove Download (or Free up space), or make them online-only in the provider's app.

title: App cache
owner: The app named in the path
what: Temporary files a sandboxed app keeps to work faster.
ifDeleted: The app rebuilds what it needs.
howToClean: Quit the app first.

title: App caches
owner: The app named in the path
what: Temporary files apps keep to work faster.
ifDeleted: Apps rebuild what they need. Some may be slower the first time.
howToClean: Quit the app first.

title: Logs
what: Log files apps write for troubleshooting.
ifDeleted: Nothing you'd notice. Only past troubleshooting info is lost.

title: Saved window state
what: Which windows each app had open, so it can restore them.
ifDeleted: Apps open with fresh windows next time.

title: Trash
what: Files you already moved to the Trash. They take space until you empty it.
ifDeleted: Gone for good.
howToClean: Finder › Empty Trash.

title: Browser profile
what: Bookmarks, history, saved passwords and extensions.
ifDeleted: You lose everything that isn't synced to your browser account.
howToClean: Clear cached files from inside the browser (Settings › Privacy › Clear browsing data › Cached images and files).

title: Claude app data
what: Your Claude sessions, settings and sign-in.
ifDeleted: Claude signs you out and loses local sessions and settings.
howToClean: Claude › Settings › This computer › Storage shows what's using space and has Clear cache.

title: Claude Code data
what: Claude Code settings, chat history, plugins and memory.
ifDeleted: Claude Code loses its settings and history.

title: Codex data
what: Codex settings, chat history and logs.
ifDeleted: Codex loses its settings and history.
howToClean: Look inside: sessions holds old chats, which are usually the bulk.

title: Gemini CLI / Antigravity data
what: Settings, chat history and agent files for Google's AI coding tools.
ifDeleted: Those tools lose their settings and history.

title: Antigravity editor data
what: Extensions and settings for the Antigravity code editor.
ifDeleted: The editor loses its extensions until you reinstall them.

title: Dart / Flutter package cache
what: Packages downloaded for your Dart and Flutter projects.
ifDeleted: Downloaded again on the next `flutter pub get`.
howToClean: Run `flutter pub cache clean` (or `dart pub cache clean`).

title: Build tool folder
owner: Gradle, Maven, Cargo, Yarn, Bun or Go
what: The tool's settings plus its download cache, which is usually most of the size.
ifDeleted: The tool loses its settings and may stop working (Cargo and Bun keep their programs here).
howToClean: Open it and delete the cache folder inside instead; Roomy marks it Safe.

title: Command-line tool caches
owner: The tool named in the path
what: Downloads and temporary files command-line tools keep.
ifDeleted: Most tools download what they need again, but some keep AI models here that are large to re-download.
howToClean: Open it and check each folder.

title: Locally installed tools
owner: Command-line tools (Claude Code, pipx, uv and others)
what: Programs installed just for you (in bin) and their data (in share).
ifDeleted: Those tools stop working.

title: Xcode
what: Apple's developer tools. Often more than 10 GB per copy.
ifDeleted: You can't build Apple-platform apps until you reinstall it.
howToClean: Keep one version and delete older Xcode copies.

title: App
what: An installed app.
ifDeleted: The app is removed. Its settings and data in ~/Library stay behind unless you remove them too.
howToClean: If you don't use it, move it to the Trash. Apps with their own uninstaller (Adobe, antivirus, VPNs) should use it instead.

title: Developer tool data
what: Data developer tools keep: builds, simulators, symbols.
ifDeleted: Depends on the folder. Look inside for the specific parts.

title: Shared app data
owner: Apps from the developer named in the path
what: Data shared between related apps, such as an app and its widgets.
ifDeleted: Those apps may lose data or settings.

title: App's private folder
owner: The app named in the path
what: A sandboxed app's own folder: its documents, settings and caches.
ifDeleted: That app loses its data and settings. If the app is already uninstalled, this is a leftover and usually safe to delete.

title: App data
owner: The app named in the path
what: Data an app saves: settings, databases, downloads.
ifDeleted: The app may reset or lose data. If the app is already uninstalled, this is a leftover and usually safe to delete.

title: Library
what: Support files macOS and your apps keep for you.
ifDeleted: Depends on the folder. Look inside rather than deleting whole folders here.

title: Downloads
what: Files you downloaded.
ifDeleted: Only what you remove is gone. Old installers, videos and archives are the usual space hogs.

title: Your files
what: Your own documents, images, videos and music.
ifDeleted: Gone once you empty the Trash, unless you have a backup.
howToClean: Look for old videos, screen recordings and large archives.

title: macOS
what: Part of macOS, protected by the system.
ifDeleted: macOS won't let you, and you wouldn't want to.

title: Shared support files
what: Files shared by all users: fonts, audio plugins, printer drivers, app helpers.
ifDeleted: Apps or devices that rely on them stop working.
